body:
Found by the post-arc audit, 2026-08-13. Four merged PRs added user-facing capability and none
grew the spec: #385 (T85, loam register --stock), #361 (T104, the front-door greeting), #371
(T110, the listing door), #367 (T102, pen provisioning -- partial, its ticket is still open). None
had a working spec in .adlc/specs/ either, so there is nothing to transcribe: the sections must be
written FROM the landed code and the PR bodies, which is backwards from the process and is why this
is a ticket rather than a follow-up commit.

WHY IT MATTERS. spec/ is the record of what IS; a capability that lives only in its PR body is
invisible to the next design stage, and the capabilities book cannot be red for a section that was
never written -- test/site/capabilities.test.ts passes vacuously today. The promise record and the
book drift together.

THE WORK, per surface: write the spec/NN-slug.md section with its Provenance footer (the PR link +
implementation note), add the SPEC.md index row, add the capabilities chapter and its
{says, spec, proof} claim. T102's section waits for its ticket to close or covers only the landed
half, saying so. Numbering: pick unclaimed NN values against the reserved-number rule; do not
renumber anything.

MERGE: Myk's, every time -- these sections state what the system promises, and writing them
post-hoc is exactly when an overclaim slips in. The drafts should cite their rails the way a
working spec would, so the book claims are transcription.

RAILS: test/site/capabilities.test.ts goes red if a section lands without its chapter -- that
existing rail is the enforcement once the sections exist.
title: Four landings owe the spec their sections — the stock shelf, the front door, the listing door, and pens
